   192	RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalHydrationData ReadHydrationData(
   193	    pqxx::transaction_base& transaction,
   194	    const pqxx::row& row)
   195	{
   196	    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalHydrationData data;
   197	    data.proposalContractVersion =
   198	        row["proposal_contract_version"].as<int>();
   199	    data.proposalIdentityCanonical =
   200	        row["proposal_identity_canonical"].as<std::string>();
   201	    data.proposalIdentityHash =
   202	        row["proposal_identity_hash"].as<std::string>();
   203	    data.assessmentContractVersion =
   204	        row["assessment_contract_version"].as<int>();
   205	    data.assessmentCanonicalText =
   206	        row["assessment_identity_canonical"].as<std::string>();
   207	    data.assessmentIdentityHash =
   208	        row["assessment_identity_hash"].as<std::string>();
   209	    data.policyContractVersion = row["policy_contract_version"].as<int>();
   210	    data.policyCanonicalText =
   211	        row["policy_identity_canonical"].as<std::string>();
   212	    data.policyIdentityHash = row["policy_identity_hash"].as<std::string>();
   213	    data.policyDecisionContractVersion =
   214	        row["policy_decision_contract_version"].as<int>();
   215	    data.policyDecisionCanonicalText =
   216	        row["policy_decision_identity_canonical"].as<std::string>();
   217	    data.policyDecisionIdentityHash =
   218	        row["policy_decision_identity_hash"].as<std::string>();
   219	    data.campaignApprovalId = row["campaign_approval_id"].as<long long>();
   220	    data.campaignIdentityCanonical =
   221	        row["campaign_identity_canonical"].as<std::string>();
   222	    data.campaignIdentityHash =
   223	        row["campaign_identity_hash"].as<std::string>();
   224	    data.materializationId = row["materialization_id"].as<long long>();
   225	    data.materializationCampaignApprovalId =
   226	        row["materialization_campaign_approval_id"].as<long long>();
   227	    data.materializationCampaignIdentityHash =
   228	        row["materialization_campaign_identity_hash"].as<std::string>();
   229	    data.materializationContractVersion =
   230	        row["materialization_contract_version"].as<int>();
   231	    data.memberCount = row["member_count"].as<int>();
   232	    data.materializationIdentityCanonical =
   233	        row["materialization_identity_canonical"].as<std::string>();
   234	    data.materializationIdentityHash =
   235	        row["materialization_identity_hash"].as<std::string>();
   236	
   237	    if (row["evidence_sufficiency"].as<std::string>() != "sufficient" ||
   238	        row["campaign_interpretation"].as<std::string>() != "favorable" ||
   239	        row["follow_up_eligibility"].as<std::string>() !=
   240	            "eligible_for_operator_review" ||
   241	        row["proposal_reason"].as<std::string>() !=
   242	            "eligible_favorable_policy_decision")
   243	        throw std::runtime_error("persisted_classification_invalid");
   244	    data.evidenceSufficiency = EvidenceSufficiency::Sufficient;
   245	    data.campaignInterpretation = Interpretation::Favorable;
   246	    data.followUpEligibility = Eligibility::EligibleForOperatorReview;
   247	    data.followUpAuthorized = row["follow_up_authorized"].as<bool>();
   248	    data.reason = ProposalReason::EligibleFavorablePolicyDecision;
   249	
   250	    const long long persistedId =
   251	        row["recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_id"].as<long long>();
   252	    const pqxx::result memberRows = transaction.exec(
   253	        "SELECT " + MemberColumns() + " FROM "
   254	        "experiment_recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_member "
   255	        "WHERE recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_id=$1 "
   256	        "ORDER BY member_ordinal ASC;", pqxx::params{persistedId});
   257	    data.members.reserve(memberRows.size());
   258	    for (const auto& member : memberRows)
   259	    {
   260	        const std::optional<long long> expectedExperimentId =
   261	            member["expected_experiment_id"].is_null()
   262	                ? std::nullopt
   263	                : std::optional<long long>{
   264	                      member["expected_experiment_id"].as<long long>()};
   265	        data.members.emplace_back(member["member_ordinal"].as<int>(),
   266	            member["materialization_member_id"].as<long long>(),
   267	            member["ranking_member_id"].as<long long>(),
   268	            member["recommendation_id"].as<long long>(),
   269	            member["source_experiment_id"].as<long long>(),
   270	            member["conversion_proposal_id"].as<long long>(),
   271	            expectedExperimentId);
   272	    }
   273	    if (static_cast<int>(data.members.size()) != data.memberCount)
   274	        throw std::runtime_error("persisted_member_count_mismatch");
   275	    return data;
   276	}
   277	
   278	Persisted MapProposal(
   279	    pqxx::transaction_base& transaction,
   280	    const pqxx::row& row)
   281	{
   282	    try
   283	    {
   284	        const long long id =
   285	            row["recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_id"]
   286	                .as<long long>();
   287	        const int collisionOrdinal =
   288	            row["proposal_identity_hash_collision_ordinal"].as<int>();
   289	        const std::string createdAt = row["created_at"].as<std::string>();
   290	        if (id <= 0 || collisionOrdinal < 0 || createdAt.empty())
   291	            throw std::runtime_error("persisted_metadata_invalid");
   292	        auto proposal =
   293	            RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalPersistenceBuilder::
   294	                Hydrate(ReadHydrationData(transaction, row));
   295	        return Persisted(id, collisionOrdinal, std::move(proposal),
   296	            createdAt);
   297	    }
   298	    catch (const std::exception& error)
   299	    {
   300	        throw std::runtime_error(
   301	            "invalid_persisted_recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal:" +
   302	            std::string(error.what()));
   303	    }
   304	}
   305	
   306	std::optional<Persisted> FindByIdentity(
   307	    pqxx::transaction_base& transaction,
   308	    const std::string& canonical)
   309	{
   310	    const pqxx::result rows = transaction.exec(
   311	        "SELECT " + ProposalColumns() + " FROM "
   312	        "experiment_recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal WHERE "
   313	        "proposal_identity_hash=$1 AND proposal_identity_canonical=$2 "
   314	        "LIMIT 2;",
   315	        pqxx::params{RecommendationCanonicalHash(canonical), canonical});
   316	    if (rows.empty()) return std::nullopt;
   317	    if (rows.size() != 1)
   318	        throw std::runtime_error(
   319	            "recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_duplicate_identity");
   320	    return MapProposal(transaction, rows.one_row());
   321	}

   205	RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalValidationView
   206	MakeRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalValidationView(
   207	    const Assessment& assessment,
   208	    const Decision& policyDecision)
   209	{
   210	    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalValidationView view;
   211	    view.assessmentContractVersion = assessment.identity.contractVersion;
   212	    view.assessmentCanonicalText = assessment.identity.canonicalText;
   213	    view.assessmentIdentityHash = assessment.identity.hash;
   214	    view.policyContractVersion =
   215	        policyDecision.policy.identity.contractVersion;
   216	    view.policyCanonicalText = policyDecision.policy.identity.canonicalText;
   217	    view.policyIdentityHash = policyDecision.policy.identity.hash;
   218	    view.policyDecisionContractVersion =
   219	        policyDecision.identity.contractVersion;
   220	    view.policyDecisionCanonicalText = policyDecision.identity.canonicalText;
   221	    view.policyDecisionIdentityHash = policyDecision.identity.hash;
   222	    view.decisionAssessmentContractVersion =
   223	        policyDecision.assessmentContractVersion;
   224	    view.decisionAssessmentCanonicalText =
   225	        policyDecision.assessmentCanonicalText;
   226	    view.decisionAssessmentIdentityHash =
   227	        policyDecision.assessmentIdentityHash;
   228	    view.assessmentCampaignIdentity =
   229	        CampaignValidationView(assessment.campaignIdentity);
   230	    view.decisionCampaignIdentity =
   231	        CampaignValidationView(policyDecision.campaignIdentity);
   232	    view.assessmentMaterializationIdentity =
   233	        MaterializationValidationView(assessment.materializationIdentity);
   234	    view.decisionMaterializationIdentity =
   235	        MaterializationValidationView(policyDecision.materializationIdentity);
   236	    view.assessmentSummaryMemberCount = assessment.summary.memberCount;
   237	    view.decisionSummaryMemberCount = policyDecision.summary.memberCount;
   238	    view.assessmentMembers.reserve(assessment.members.size());
   239	    for (const auto& member : assessment.members)
   240	        view.assessmentMembers.push_back(MemberValidationView(member.identity));
   241	    view.decisionMembers.reserve(policyDecision.members.size());
   242	    for (const auto& member : policyDecision.members)
   243	        view.decisionMembers.push_back(MemberValidationView(member.identity));
   244	    view.evidenceSufficiency = policyDecision.summary.evidenceSufficiency;
   245	    view.campaignInterpretation =
   246	        policyDecision.summary.campaignInterpretation;
   247	    view.followUpEligibility = policyDecision.summary.followUpEligibility;
   248	    view.followUpAuthorized = policyDecision.summary.followUpAuthorized;
   249	    return view;
   250	}
   251	
   252	void ValidateRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalInput(
   253	    const RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalValidationView& view)
   254	{
   255	    if (view.assessmentContractVersion !=
   256	            kRecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentContractVersion ||
   257	        view.decisionAssessmentContractVersion !=
   258	            kRecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentContractVersion)
   259	        throw std::invalid_argument("assessment_contract_unsupported");
   260	    if (view.policyContractVersion !=
   261	        kRecommendationCampaignOutcomePolicyContractVersion)
   262	        throw std::invalid_argument("policy_contract_unsupported");
   263	    if (view.policyDecisionContractVersion !=
   264	        kRecommendationCampaignOutcomePolicyDecisionContractVersion)
   265	        throw std::invalid_argument("policy_decision_contract_unsupported");
   266	
   267	    if (!ValidCanonicalIdentity(
   268	            view.assessmentCanonicalText, view.assessmentIdentityHash))
   269	        throw std::invalid_argument("assessment_identity_mismatch");
   270	    if (!ValidCanonicalIdentity(
   271	            view.policyCanonicalText, view.policyIdentityHash))
   272	        throw std::invalid_argument("policy_identity_mismatch");
   273	    if (!ValidCanonicalIdentity(view.policyDecisionCanonicalText,
   274	            view.policyDecisionIdentityHash))
   275	        throw std::invalid_argument("policy_decision_identity_mismatch");
   276	
   277	    if (!ValidCampaignIdentity(view.assessmentCampaignIdentity) ||
   278	        !ValidCampaignIdentity(view.decisionCampaignIdentity) ||
   279	        view.assessmentCampaignIdentity != view.decisionCampaignIdentity)
   280	        throw std::invalid_argument("campaign_identity_mismatch");
   281	    if (!ValidMaterializationIdentity(
   282	            view.assessmentMaterializationIdentity) ||
   283	        !ValidMaterializationIdentity(view.decisionMaterializationIdentity) ||
   284	        view.assessmentMaterializationIdentity !=
   285	            view.decisionMaterializationIdentity ||
   286	        view.assessmentMaterializationIdentity.campaignApprovalId !=
   287	            view.assessmentCampaignIdentity.campaignApprovalId ||
   288	        view.assessmentMaterializationIdentity.campaignIdentityHash !=
   289	            view.assessmentCampaignIdentity.identityHash)
   290	        throw std::invalid_argument("materialization_identity_mismatch");
   291	
   292	    const std::size_t assessmentMemberCount =
   293	        view.assessmentMembers.size();
   294	    if (assessmentMemberCount == 0 ||
   295	        view.decisionMembers.size() != assessmentMemberCount ||
   296	        view.assessmentSummaryMemberCount !=
   297	            static_cast<int>(assessmentMemberCount) ||
   298	        view.decisionSummaryMemberCount !=
   299	            static_cast<int>(assessmentMemberCount) ||
   300	        view.assessmentMaterializationIdentity.memberCount !=
   301	            static_cast<int>(assessmentMemberCount))
   302	        throw std::invalid_argument("member_count_mismatch");
   303	    if (view.assessmentMembers != view.decisionMembers)
   304	        throw std::invalid_argument("member_identity_mismatch");
   305	    std::set<long long> materializationMemberIds;
   306	    std::set<long long> rankingMemberIds;
   307	    std::set<long long> recommendationIds;
   308	    std::set<long long> proposalIds;
   309	    for (std::size_t index = 0; index < assessmentMemberCount; ++index)
   310	    {
   311	        const auto& member = view.assessmentMembers[index];
   312	        if (member.memberOrdinal != static_cast<int>(index) + 1 ||
   313	            member.materializationMemberId <= 0 ||
   314	            member.rankingMemberId <= 0 || member.recommendationId <= 0 ||
   315	            member.sourceExperimentId <= 0 || member.proposalId <= 0 ||
   316	            (member.expectedExperimentId &&
   317	                *member.expectedExperimentId <= 0) ||
   318	            !materializationMemberIds
   319	                 .insert(member.materializationMemberId).second ||
   320	            !rankingMemberIds.insert(member.rankingMemberId).second ||
   321	            !recommendationIds.insert(member.recommendationId).second ||
   322	            !proposalIds.insert(member.proposalId).second)
   323	            throw std::invalid_argument("member_identity_mismatch");
   324	    }
   325	
   326	    if (view.decisionAssessmentContractVersion !=
   327	            view.assessmentContractVersion ||
   328	        view.decisionAssessmentCanonicalText !=
   329	            view.assessmentCanonicalText ||
   330	        view.decisionAssessmentIdentityHash != view.assessmentIdentityHash)
   331	        throw std::invalid_argument("assessment_identity_mismatch");
   332	
   333	    if (view.followUpAuthorized)
   334	        throw std::invalid_argument(
   335	            "follow_up_authorization_must_be_false");
   336	    if (view.followUpEligibility !=
   337	        Eligibility::EligibleForOperatorReview)
   338	        throw std::invalid_argument(
   339	            "decision_not_eligible_for_operator_review");
   340	    if (view.campaignInterpretation != Interpretation::Favorable)
   341	        throw std::invalid_argument(
   342	            "favorable_campaign_interpretation_required");
   343	}

   345	void ValidateRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalCanonicalSize(
   346	    std::size_t canonicalTextBytes)
   347	{
   348	    if (canonicalTextBytes >
   349	        kMaximumRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalCanonicalTextBytes)
   350	        throw std::length_error("proposal_canonical_size_exceeded");
   351	}

   353	RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalIdentity::
   354	    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalIdentity(

   357	        std::string hashValue)

   378	RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalSummary::

   384	        bool followUpAuthorizedValue,
   385	        int memberCountValue,

   400	            "recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_summary_invariant_failed");
   401	}

   423	      assessmentContractVersion(assessmentContractVersionValue),
   424	      assessmentCanonicalText(std::move(assessmentCanonicalTextValue)),
   425	      assessmentIdentityHash(std::move(assessmentIdentityHashValue)),
   426	      policyContractVersion(policyContractVersionValue),
   427	      policyCanonicalText(std::move(policyCanonicalTextValue)),
   428	      policyIdentityHash(std::move(policyIdentityHashValue)),
   429	      policyDecisionContractVersion(policyDecisionContractVersionValue),
   430	      policyDecisionCanonicalText(
   431	          std::move(policyDecisionCanonicalTextValue)),
   432	      policyDecisionIdentityHash(
   433	          std::move(policyDecisionIdentityHashValue)),
   434	      campaignIdentity(std::move(campaignIdentityValue)),
   435	      materializationIdentity(std::move(materializationIdentityValue)),
   436	      memberCount(memberCountValue),
   437	      summary(std::move(summaryValue)),
   438	      members(std::move(membersValue))
   439	{
   440	    if (assessmentContractVersion !=
   441	            kRecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentContractVersion ||
   442	        policyContractVersion !=
   443	            kRecommendationCampaignOutcomePolicyContractVersion ||
   444	        policyDecisionContractVersion !=
   445	            kRecommendationCampaignOutcomePolicyDecisionContractVersion ||
   446	        !ValidCanonicalIdentity(
   447	            assessmentCanonicalText, assessmentIdentityHash) ||
   448	        !ValidCanonicalIdentity(policyCanonicalText, policyIdentityHash) ||
   449	        !ValidCanonicalIdentity(
   450	            policyDecisionCanonicalText, policyDecisionIdentityHash) ||
   451	        memberCount != static_cast<int>(members.size()) ||
   452	        summary.memberCount != memberCount)
   453	        throw std::logic_error(
   454	            "recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_invariant_failed");
   455	    const std::string expectedCanonical = ProposalCanonicalText(
   456	        assessmentContractVersion, assessmentCanonicalText,
   457	        assessmentIdentityHash, policyContractVersion, policyCanonicalText,
   458	        policyIdentityHash, policyDecisionContractVersion,
   459	        policyDecisionCanonicalText, policyDecisionIdentityHash,
   460	        campaignIdentity, materializationIdentity, summary, members);
   461	    if (identity.canonicalText != expectedCanonical ||
   462	        identity.hash != RecommendationCanonicalHash(expectedCanonical))
   463	        throw std::logic_error(
   464	            "recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_identity_payload_mismatch");
   465	}
   466	
   467	struct RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalBuilder
   468	{
   469	    static RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposal Build(
   470	        const Assessment& assessment,
   471	        const Decision& policyDecision)
   472	    {
   473	        ValidateRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalInput(
   474	            MakeRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalValidationView(
   475	                assessment, policyDecision));
   476	
   477	        std::vector<ProposalMember> members;
   478	        members.reserve(assessment.members.size());
   479	        for (const auto& member : assessment.members)
   480	            members.push_back(ProposalMember(member.identity));
   481	
   482	        RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalSummary summary(
   483	            policyDecision.summary.evidenceSufficiency,
   484	            policyDecision.summary.campaignInterpretation,
   485	            policyDecision.summary.followUpEligibility,
   486	            policyDecision.summary.followUpAuthorized,
   487	            static_cast<int>(members.size()),
   488	            {ProposalReason::EligibleFavorablePolicyDecision});
   489	        std::string canonical = ProposalCanonicalText(
   490	            assessment.identity.contractVersion,
   491	            assessment.identity.canonicalText, assessment.identity.hash,
   492	            policyDecision.policy.identity.contractVersion,
   493	            policyDecision.policy.identity.canonicalText,
   494	            policyDecision.policy.identity.hash,
   495	            policyDecision.identity.contractVersion,
   496	            policyDecision.identity.canonicalText,
   497	            policyDecision.identity.hash, assessment.campaignIdentity,
   498	            assessment.materializationIdentity, summary, members);
   499	        ValidateRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalCanonicalSize(
   500	            canonical.size());
   501	        RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalIdentity identity(
   502	            kRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalContractVersion,
   503	            canonical, RecommendationCanonicalHash(canonical));
   504	        return RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposal(
   505	            std::move(identity), assessment.identity.contractVersion,
   506	            assessment.identity.canonicalText, assessment.identity.hash,
   507	            policyDecision.policy.identity.contractVersion,
   508	            policyDecision.policy.identity.canonicalText,
   509	            policyDecision.policy.identity.hash,
   510	            policyDecision.identity.contractVersion,
   511	            policyDecision.identity.canonicalText,
   512	            policyDecision.identity.hash, assessment.campaignIdentity,
   513	            assessment.materializationIdentity,
   514	            static_cast<int>(members.size()), std::move(summary),
   515	            std::move(members));
   516	    }
   517	};
   518	
   519	RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposal
   520	BuildRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposal(
   521	    const Assessment& assessment,
   522	    const Decision& policyDecision)
   523	{
   524	    return RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalBuilder::Build(
   525	        assessment, policyDecision);
   526	}
   527	
   528	std::string RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReasonText(
   529	    RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalReason value)
   530	{
   531	    switch (value)
   532	    {
   533	        case ProposalReason::EligibleFavorablePolicyDecision:
   534	            return "eligible_favorable_policy_decision";
   535	    }
   536	    throw std::invalid_argument(
   537	        "recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_reason_invalid");
   538	}

   120	        proposal_identity_hash ~ '^fnv1a64:[0-9a-f]{16}$'),
   121	    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
   122	    CONSTRAINT recommendation_campaign_materialization_member_rank_fkey
   123	        FOREIGN KEY (recommendation_ranking_member_id, recommendation_id,
   124	                     source_experiment_id)
   125	        REFERENCES experiment_recommendation_ranking_member(
   126	            recommendation_ranking_member_id, recommendation_id,
   127	            source_experiment_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
   128	    CONSTRAINT recommendation_campaign_materialization_member_proposal_fkey
   129	        FOREIGN KEY (recommendation_conversion_proposal_id,
   130	                     recommendation_id, source_experiment_id)
   131	        REFERENCES experiment_recommendation_conversion_proposal(
   132	            recommendation_conversion_proposal_id, recommendation_id,
   133	            source_experiment_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
   134	    CONSTRAINT recommendation_campaign_materialization_member_ordinal_uidx
   135	        UNIQUE (recommendation_campaign_materialization_id, member_ordinal),
   136	    CONSTRAINT recommendation_campaign_materialization_member_rank_uidx
   137	        UNIQUE (recommendation_campaign_materialization_id,
   138	                recommendation_ranking_member_id),
   139	    CONSTRAINT recommendation_campaign_materialization_member_proposal_uidx
   140	        UNIQUE (recommendation_campaign_materialization_id,
   141	                recommendation_conversion_proposal_id)
   142	);
   143	
   144	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION
   145	enforce_recommendation_campaign_materialization_manifest_insert()
   146	RETURNS trigger
   147	LANGUAGE plpgsql
   148	SECURITY INVOKER
   149	AS $$
   150	BEGIN
   151	    PERFORM 1
   152	    FROM experiment_recommendation_campaign_approval approval
   153	    WHERE approval.recommendation_campaign_approval_id =
   154	              NEW.recommendation_campaign_approval_id
   155	      AND approval.decision = 'approved'
   156	      AND NEW.approval_decision = approval.decision
   157	      AND NEW.approval_identity_canonical =
   158	              approval.approval_identity_canonical
   159	      AND NEW.approval_identity_hash = approval.approval_identity_hash
   160	      AND NEW.recommendation_ranking_snapshot_id =
   161	              approval.recommendation_ranking_snapshot_id
   162	      AND NEW.ranking_snapshot_identity_canonical =
   163	              approval.ranking_snapshot_identity_canonical
   164	      AND NEW.ranking_snapshot_identity_hash =
   165	              approval.ranking_snapshot_identity_hash
   166	      AND NEW.planning_policy_canonical = approval.planning_policy_canonical
   167	      AND NEW.planning_policy_hash = approval.planning_policy_hash
   168	      AND NEW.planning_scope_canonical = approval.planning_scope_canonical
   169	      AND NEW.campaign_plan_identity_canonical =
   170	              approval.campaign_plan_identity_canonical
   171	      AND NEW.campaign_plan_identity_hash =
   172	              approval.campaign_plan_identity_hash
   173	      AND NEW.campaign_review_identity_canonical =
   174	              approval.campaign_review_identity_canonical
   175	      AND NEW.campaign_review_identity_hash =
   176	              approval.campaign_review_identity_hash
   177	      AND NEW.approval_reviewer_identity = approval.reviewer_identity
   178	      AND NEW.approval_reason_text = approval.reason_text
   179	      AND NEW.selected_member_count = approval.selected_count;
   180	    IF NOT FOUND THEN
   181	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'campaign materialization approval provenance mismatch'
   182	            USING ERRCODE = '23514',
   183	                  CONSTRAINT =
   184	                      'recommendation_campaign_materialization_authority_check';
   185	    END IF;
   186	    RETURN NEW;
   187	END;
   188	$$;
   189	
   190	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION
   191	enforce_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member_insert()
   192	RETURNS trigger
   193	LANGUAGE plpgsql
   194	SECURITY INVOKER
   195	AS $$
   196	BEGIN
   197	    PERFORM 1
   198	    FROM experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization materialization
   199	    JOIN experiment_recommendation_ranking_member ranking_member
   200	      ON ranking_member.recommendation_ranking_member_id =
   201	             NEW.recommendation_ranking_member_id
   202	     AND ranking_member.recommendation_ranking_snapshot_id =
   203	             materialization.recommendation_ranking_snapshot_id
   204	     AND ranking_member.recommendation_id = NEW.recommendation_id
   205	     AND ranking_member.source_experiment_id = NEW.source_experiment_id
   206	     AND ranking_member.global_ordinal = NEW.ranking_position
   207	    JOIN experiment_recommendation_conversion_proposal proposal
   208	      ON proposal.recommendation_conversion_proposal_id =
   209	             NEW.recommendation_conversion_proposal_id
   210	     AND proposal.recommendation_id = NEW.recommendation_id
   211	     AND proposal.source_experiment_id = NEW.source_experiment_id
   212	     AND proposal.conversion_identity_canonical =
   213	             NEW.proposal_identity_canonical
   214	     AND proposal.conversion_identity_hash = NEW.proposal_identity_hash
   215	    WHERE materialization.recommendation_campaign_materialization_id =
   216	              NEW.recommendation_campaign_materialization_id
   217	      AND NEW.member_ordinal <= materialization.selected_member_count;
   218	    IF NOT FOUND THEN
   219	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'campaign materialization member provenance mismatch'
   220	            USING ERRCODE = '23514',
   221	                  CONSTRAINT =
   222	                      'recommendation_campaign_materialization_member_authority_check';
   223	    END IF;
   224	    RETURN NEW;
   225	END;
   226	$$;
   227	
   228	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION
   229	enforce_recommendation_campaign_materialization_complete()
   230	RETURNS trigger
     1	DO $$
     2	BEGIN
     3	    IF to_regclass('experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization') IS NULL
     4	       OR to_regclass(
     5	           'experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member') IS NULL
     6	    THEN
     7	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'campaign materialization tables missing';
     8	    END IF;
     9	    IF (SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns
    10	        WHERE table_schema=current_schema()
    11	          AND table_name='experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization'
    12	          AND column_name IN (
    13	              'recommendation_campaign_materialization_id',
    14	              'recommendation_campaign_approval_id',
    15	              'materialization_identity_canonical',
    16	              'materialization_identity_hash','created_at')) <> 5 THEN
    17	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'campaign materialization columns missing';
    18	    END IF;
    19	    IF (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_constraint
    20	        WHERE conrelid='experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization'::regclass
    21	          AND contype='f') <> 2 THEN
    22	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'manifest restrictive foreign keys missing';
    23	    END IF;
    24	    IF (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_constraint
    25	        WHERE conrelid=
    26	          'experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member'::regclass
    27	          AND contype='f') <> 5 THEN
    28	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'member restrictive foreign keys missing';
    29	    END IF;
    30	    IF (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_trigger
    31	        WHERE tgrelid IN (
    32	            'experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization'::regclass,
    33	            'experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member'::regclass)
    34	          AND NOT tgisinternal
    35	          AND tgname LIKE 'enforce_recommendation_campaign_materialization_%')
    36	       <> 3 THEN
    37	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'materialization enforcement triggers missing';
    38	    END IF;
    39	    IF has_table_privilege(
    40	        'pqxx','experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization','UPDATE')
    41	       OR has_table_privilege(
    42	        'pqxx','experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization','DELETE')
    43	       OR has_table_privilege(
    44	        'pqxx','experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization','TRUNCATE')
    45	       OR has_table_privilege(
    46	        'pqxx','experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member','UPDATE')
    47	       OR has_table_privilege(
    48	        'pqxx','experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member','DELETE')
    49	       OR has_table_privilege(
    50	        'pqxx','experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member','TRUNCATE')
    51	    THEN
    52	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'append-only runtime privilege violated';
    53	    END IF;
    54	    IF EXISTS (
    55	        SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.role_table_grants
    56	        WHERE table_schema=current_schema() AND grantee='PUBLIC'
    57	          AND table_name IN (
    58	            'experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization',
    59	            'experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member'))
    60	    THEN
    61	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'PUBLIC materialization privilege present';
    62	    END IF;
    63	    IF has_function_privilege(
    64	           'pqxx',
    65	           'enforce_recommendation_campaign_materialization_manifest_insert()',
    66	           'EXECUTE')
    67	       OR has_function_privilege(
    68	           'pqxx',
    69	           'enforce_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member_insert()',
    70	           'EXECUTE')
    71	       OR has_function_privilege(
    72	           'pqxx',
    73	           'enforce_recommendation_campaign_materialization_complete()',
    74	           'EXECUTE')
    75	    THEN
    76	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'runtime trigger-function execution privilege present';
    77	    END IF;
    78	END $$;

    48	        hash == RecommendationCanonicalHash(canonicalText);

    90	        ValidCanonicalIdentity(

   252	void ValidateRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalInput(
   253	    const RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposalValidationView& view)
   254	{
   255	    if (view.assessmentContractVersion !=
   256	            kRecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentContractVersion ||
   257	        view.decisionAssessmentContractVersion !=
   258	            kRecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessmentContractVersion)
   259	        throw std::invalid_argument("assessment_contract_unsupported");
   260	    if (view.policyContractVersion !=
   261	        kRecommendationCampaignOutcomePolicyContractVersion)
   262	        throw std::invalid_argument("policy_contract_unsupported");
   263	    if (view.policyDecisionContractVersion !=
   264	        kRecommendationCampaignOutcomePolicyDecisionContractVersion)
   265	        throw std::invalid_argument("policy_decision_contract_unsupported");
   266	
   267	    if (!ValidCanonicalIdentity(
   268	            view.assessmentCanonicalText, view.assessmentIdentityHash))
   269	        throw std::invalid_argument("assessment_identity_mismatch");
   270	    if (!ValidCanonicalIdentity(
   271	            view.policyCanonicalText, view.policyIdentityHash))
   272	        throw std::invalid_argument("policy_identity_mismatch");
   273	    if (!ValidCanonicalIdentity(view.policyDecisionCanonicalText,
   274	            view.policyDecisionIdentityHash))
   275	        throw std::invalid_argument("policy_decision_identity_mismatch");
   276	
   277	    if (!ValidCampaignIdentity(view.assessmentCampaignIdentity) ||
   278	        !ValidCampaignIdentity(view.decisionCampaignIdentity) ||
   279	        view.assessmentCampaignIdentity != view.decisionCampaignIdentity)
   280	        throw std::invalid_argument("campaign_identity_mismatch");
   281	    if (!ValidMaterializationIdentity(
   282	            view.assessmentMaterializationIdentity) ||
   283	        !ValidMaterializationIdentity(view.decisionMaterializationIdentity) ||
   284	        view.assessmentMaterializationIdentity !=
   285	            view.decisionMaterializationIdentity ||
   286	        view.assessmentMaterializationIdentity.campaignApprovalId !=
   287	            view.assessmentCampaignIdentity.campaignApprovalId ||
   288	        view.assessmentMaterializationIdentity.campaignIdentityHash !=
   289	            view.assessmentCampaignIdentity.identityHash)
   290	        throw std::invalid_argument("materialization_identity_mismatch");
   291	
   292	    const std::size_t assessmentMemberCount =
   293	        view.assessmentMembers.size();
   294	    if (assessmentMemberCount == 0 ||
   295	        view.decisionMembers.size() != assessmentMemberCount ||
   296	        view.assessmentSummaryMemberCount !=
   297	            static_cast<int>(assessmentMemberCount) ||
   298	        view.decisionSummaryMemberCount !=
   299	            static_cast<int>(assessmentMemberCount) ||
   300	        view.assessmentMaterializationIdentity.memberCount !=
   301	            static_cast<int>(assessmentMemberCount))
   302	        throw std::invalid_argument("member_count_mismatch");
   303	    if (view.assessmentMembers != view.decisionMembers)
   304	        throw std::invalid_argument("member_identity_mismatch");
   305	    std::set<long long> materializationMemberIds;
   306	    std::set<long long> rankingMemberIds;
   307	    std::set<long long> recommendationIds;
   308	    std::set<long long> proposalIds;
   309	    for (std::size_t index = 0; index < assessmentMemberCount; ++index)
   310	    {
   311	        const auto& member = view.assessmentMembers[index];
   312	        if (member.memberOrdinal != static_cast<int>(index) + 1 ||
   313	            member.materializationMemberId <= 0 ||
   314	            member.rankingMemberId <= 0 || member.recommendationId <= 0 ||
   315	            member.sourceExperimentId <= 0 || member.proposalId <= 0 ||
   316	            (member.expectedExperimentId &&
   317	                *member.expectedExperimentId <= 0) ||
   318	            !materializationMemberIds
   319	                 .insert(member.materializationMemberId).second ||
   320	            !rankingMemberIds.insert(member.rankingMemberId).second ||
   321	            !recommendationIds.insert(member.recommendationId).second ||
   322	            !proposalIds.insert(member.proposalId).second)
   323	            throw std::invalid_argument("member_identity_mismatch");
   324	    }
   325	
   326	    if (view.decisionAssessmentContractVersion !=
   327	            view.assessmentContractVersion ||
   328	        view.decisionAssessmentCanonicalText !=
   329	            view.assessmentCanonicalText ||
   330	        view.decisionAssessmentIdentityHash != view.assessmentIdentityHash)
   331	        throw std::invalid_argument("assessment_identity_mismatch");
   332	
   333	    if (view.followUpAuthorized)
   334	        throw std::invalid_argument(
   335	            "follow_up_authorization_must_be_false");
   336	    if (view.followUpEligibility !=
   337	        Eligibility::EligibleForOperatorReview)
   338	        throw std::invalid_argument(
   339	            "decision_not_eligible_for_operator_review");
   340	    if (view.campaignInterpretation != Interpretation::Favorable)
   341	        throw std::invalid_argument(
   342	            "favorable_campaign_interpretation_required");
   343	}

    62	    std::ifstream input{path};

    68	bool SafeDisposableDatabaseName(const std::string& value)
    69	{
    70	    if (value.empty()) return false;
    71	    std::string lower = value;
    72	    std::transform(lower.begin(), lower.end(), lower.begin(),
    73	        [](unsigned char character)
    74	        { return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(character)); });
    75	    if (lower == "lstm") return false;
    76	    return std::all_of(value.begin(), value.end(),
    77	        [](unsigned char character)
    78	        { return std::isalnum(character) || character == '_' ||
    79	                 character == '-'; });
    80	}

     1	Phase 6A Recommendation Campaign Follow-Up Proposal
     2	====================================================
     3	
     4	Purpose and entity
     5	------------------
     6	
     7	Phase 6A defines ``RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposal``: one pure,
     8	immutable, deterministic advisory candidate for later operator review.  The
     9	name deliberately distinguishes this value from Phase 4D campaign
    10	materialization, which is an explicit persisted operation over an approved
    11	campaign.  A Phase 6A proposal materializes nothing.
    12	
    13	Exact immutable inputs
    14	----------------------
    15	
    16	The builder accepts exactly one Phase 5A
    17	``RecommendationCampaignOutcomeAssessment`` contract version 2 and one Phase
    18	5C ``RecommendationCampaignOutcomePolicyDecision`` contract version 1.  The
    19	decision must embed a Phase 5C policy contract version 1.  Phase 6A consumes
    20	only their public immutable typed values; it does not consume Step 5B formatted
    21	output, a database row, repository metadata, a scheduler value, a CLI request,
    22	or mutable operator state.
    23	
    24	Eligibility prerequisite
    25	------------------------
    26	
    27	Construction requires the validated Step 5C decision to report all of:
    28	
    29	* ``followUpEligibility == EligibleForOperatorReview``;
    30	* ``followUpAuthorized == false``; and
    31	* ``campaignInterpretation == Favorable``.
    32	
    33	Phase 6A does not derive those values, inspect Step 5A metric truth tables, or
    34	recalculate Step 5C evidence sufficiency, direction, interpretation, or
    35	eligibility.  It copies the exact decision classifications after validation.
    36	Eligibility for operator review remains neither approval nor authorization.
    37	
    38	Alignment and fail-closed validation
    39	------------------------------------
    40	
    41	Before construction, the builder validates supported assessment, policy, and
    42	policy-decision versions and each authoritative-canonical/tagged-hash pair.
    43	The decision's embedded assessment version, canonical text, and hash must
    44	equal the supplied assessment exactly.  Hash equality is never substituted
    45	for canonical-text equality.
    46	
    47	Campaign approval ID, campaign canonical identity and hash, complete
    48	materialization identity and approval linkage, member counts, and every
    49	ordered member identity must match exactly.  Member identity includes ordinal,
    50	materialization-member ID, ranking-member ID, recommendation ID, source-
    51	experiment ID, proposal ID, and optional expected-experiment ID.  Mismatch,
    52	malformed identity, unsupported version, non-eligibility, non-favorable
    53	interpretation, or authorization fails closed with a stable explicit reason.
    54	The narrow plain-data validation view exists only for safe malformed-boundary
    55	tests and cannot construct any upstream value, proposal identity, or proposal.
    56	Stable boundary reasons include ``assessment_contract_unsupported``,
    57	``policy_contract_unsupported``, ``policy_decision_contract_unsupported``,
    58	``assessment_identity_mismatch``, ``policy_identity_mismatch``,
    59	``policy_decision_identity_mismatch``, ``campaign_identity_mismatch``,
    60	``materialization_identity_mismatch``, ``member_count_mismatch``,
    61	``member_identity_mismatch``, ``decision_not_eligible_for_operator_review``,
    62	``favorable_campaign_interpretation_required``, and
    63	``follow_up_authorization_must_be_false``.
    64	
    65	Immutable output and non-authority
    66	----------------------------------
    67	
    68	The output exposes the proposal contract version; exact assessment, policy,
    69	and policy-decision version/canonical/hash triples; complete campaign and
    70	materialization identities; exact ordered members and count; copied Step 5C
    71	evidence sufficiency, campaign interpretation, eligibility, and false
    72	authorization; and the stable provenance reason
    73	``eligible_favorable_policy_decision``.
    74	
    75	The type fixes these semantics at compile time and in canonical identity:
    76	``readOnly=true``, ``databaseFree=true``, ``persistent=false``,
    77	``advisory=true``, ``authoritative=false``, ``approved=false``,
    78	``activated=false``, ``executionAuthorized=false``,
    79	``followUpAuthorized=false``, ``schedulerWork=false``, and
    80	``declaresCampaignSuccess=false``.
    81	
    82	Canonical identity grammar
    83	--------------------------
    84	
    85	Contract version 1 canonical text begins with
    86	``experiment_recommendation_campaign_follow_up_proposal_v1``.  Semicolon-
    87	named fields bind, in order:
    88	
    89	* proposal version and every fixed safety semantic;
    90	* assessment, policy, and policy-decision version/canonical/hash triples;
    91	* campaign approval ID/canonical/hash;
    92	* materialization ID, approval linkage, contract version, member count,
    93	  canonical text, and hash;
    94	* each upstream-canonical ordered member identity, including
    95	  ``expected_experiment_id``;
    96	* Step 5C evidence sufficiency, campaign interpretation, follow-up
    97	  eligibility, false decision authorization, and proposal reason.
    98	
    99	Every embedded canonical string and other delimiter-capable text is framed as
   100	``BYTE_LENGTH:VALUE``.  Integer and length formatting uses the classic locale.
   101	Canonical text is authoritative; the existing tagged FNV-1a hash is only an
   102	accelerator.  ``observedAt``, clocks, PID, CLI formatting, repository metadata,
   103	and any future approval or activation state are excluded.  Consequently,
   104	observation time cannot change identity, while every behaviorally relevant
   105	upstream identity can.
   106	
   107	Canonical-size limit
   108	--------------------
   109	
   110	Version 1 permits at most 1,048,576 canonical-text bytes.  The builder checks
   111	the completed canonical byte count before identity and proposal construction
   112	and throws ``proposal_canonical_size_exceeded`` above that inclusive ceiling.
   113	The bound limits a future review/persistence payload deliberately; it neither
   114	adds persistence nor predicts a later database schema.  Any later change to
   115	the ceiling or grammar requires a new contract version or an explicitly
   116	compatible architecture decision.
   117	
   118	Non-goals and later Phase 6 boundaries
   119	--------------------------------------
   120	
   121	Phase 6A adds no SQL, migration, table, repository, service, formatter, CLI,
   122	preview command, operator-review persistence, approval, rejection, activation,
   123	execution, scheduler work, queue, worker, campaign, recommendation, experiment,
   124	or Phase 4D materialization.  It does not claim profitability, statistical
   125	significance, repeatability, campaign success, or follow-up authorization.
   126	
   127	Persistence, explicit operator review, approval/rejection, activation, and
   128	execution remain distinct possible Phase 6B--6F concerns.  This contract does
   129	not authorize, prescribe, or partially implement any of them.

     1	# ADR-0006: Phase 6A follow-up proposal is advisory and identity-bound
     2	
     3	Status: Accepted
     4	Date: 2026-07-20
     5	Deciders: Project architecture
     6	Affected volumes: Volume VIII §§2–5, 9, 11
     7	Supersedes: None
     8	Superseded by: None
     9	
    10	## 1. Context and problem statement
    11	
    12	Phase 5A produces one immutable campaign outcome assessment, and Phase 5C
    13	produces one immutable advisory policy decision that may mark the exact
    14	assessment eligible for later operator review. That eligibility is not itself
    15	an approval, authorization, persisted review, experiment, or scheduler work
    16	item. The first Phase 6 increment needs a deterministic candidate that preserves
    17	the exact upstream identity without colliding conceptually with Phase 4D
    18	campaign materialization or silently reopening the scientific decision.
    19	
    20	## 2. Decision
    21	
    22	Phase 6A introduces the distinct pure domain entity
    23	`RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposal` with contract version 1.
    24	
    25	- It binds exactly one Phase 5A assessment v2 and one Phase 5C policy decision
    26	  v1 containing one policy v1.
    27	- Construction requires exact canonical-text, hash, campaign,
    28	  materialization, ordered-member, count, and embedded-assessment alignment.
    29	- Construction requires the Step 5C result to be eligible for operator review,
    30	  favorable, and explicitly non-authorizing. Phase 6A does not recalculate
    31	  eligibility.
    32	- Canonical text is authoritative identity. The tagged hash is only an
    33	  accelerator, and canonical text is compared even when hashes match.
    34	- Embedded canonical and delimiter-capable strings are byte-length framed.
    35	- Canonical text is independent of observation time and bounded to 1,048,576
    36	  bytes before immutable construction.
    37	- The proposal is read-only, database-free, non-persistent, advisory,
    38	  non-authoritative, unapproved, inactive, non-executing, non-authorizing,
    39	  non-scheduler work, and does not declare campaign success.
    40	- Phase 6A adds no repository, SQL, migration, service, CLI, formatter,
    41	  persisted operator review, scheduler consumer, queue, worker, or lifecycle
    42	  mutation.
    43	- Persistence, review, activation, and execution remain separate possible
    44	  later Phase 6 steps and receive no authority from this ADR.
    45	
    46	## 3. Rationale and decision drivers
    47	
    48	- Preserve exact upstream scientific and policy provenance without copying or
    49	  reinterpreting their truth tables.
    50	- Keep operator-review eligibility visibly separate from approval and action.
    51	- Make collision handling safe by retaining authoritative canonical text.
    52	- Avoid the misleading implication that an advisory proposal is Phase 4D
    53	  materialization or any experiment lifecycle request.
    54	- Keep later persistence and operational designs free to establish their own
    55	  authorities, transactions, idempotency, and concurrency contracts.
    56	
    57	## 4. Consequences
    58	
    59	### 4.1 Positive consequences
    60	
    61	- Identical validated Phase 5 inputs yield an identical Phase 6A identity
    62	  regardless of locale or observation time.
    63	- Every relevant upstream identity and explicit non-authority semantic is
    64	  reviewable in one immutable candidate.
    65	- Unsupported, mismatched, non-favorable, noneligible, authorizing, or
    66	  oversized inputs fail closed with stable reasons.
    67	- No database, scheduler, or execution dependency enters the pure boundary.
    68	
    69	### 4.2 Negative consequences and trade-offs
    70	
    71	- Binding complete upstream canonical text duplicates data and can produce a
    72	  sizable canonical value.
    73	- The 1 MiB ceiling may reject exceptionally large but otherwise valid Phase 5
    74	  decisions; changing that ceiling requires explicit versioned design.
    75	- Phase 6A alone cannot record or enact an operator decision.
    76	
    77	### 4.3 Risks and mitigations
    78	
    79	- Hash collision: compare authoritative canonical text after any hash match.
    80	- Upstream identity drift: validate exact version/canonical/hash and direct
    81	  campaign, materialization, and ordered-member fields.
    82	- Accidental authority creep: compile-time false safety flags, canonical
    83	  bindings, pure tests, and absence of persistence/scheduler integration.
    84	- Oversized future payload: reject above the fixed byte ceiling before
    85	  proposal construction.
    86	
    87	## 5. Compatibility and migration
    88	
    89	The change is additive C++ domain code and documentation. It requires no
    90	schema, data, privilege, repository, CLI, runtime, or scheduler migration and
    91	does not modify Phase 5A, 5B, or 5C contracts.
    92	
    93	## 6. Verification and operational evidence
    94	
    95	- Golden canonical text and independently fixed tagged hash.
    96	- Exact upstream alignment and stable refusal-reason tests.
    97	- Favorable/non-favorable, invariance, identity-sensitivity, IEEE edge, size,
    98	  malformed-version, and construction-access tests.
    99	- Focused normal, ASan, and UBSan runs plus Phase 4D/5 regression tests.
   100	- Both existing Xcode targets compile the source in an incremental Release
   101	  build; no Debug or clean build is required.
   102	
   103	## 7. Alternatives considered
   104	
   105	### 7.1 Generic materialization entity
   106	
   107	Rejected because it could be confused with the persisted Phase 4D operation
   108	that materializes an approved campaign into Phase 4C proposals.
   109	
   110	### 7.2 Build from Step 5B formatted output
   111	
   112	Rejected because presentation text is not the immutable typed Phase 5A/5C
   113	contract and would weaken exact identity alignment.
   114	
   115	### 7.3 Recompute Step 5C eligibility in Phase 6A
   116	
   117	Rejected because it would duplicate policy truth, risk divergence, and reopen
   118	scientific interpretation outside the versioned Step 5C owner.
   119	
   120	### 7.4 Persist or approve the proposal in Phase 6A
   121	
   122	Rejected because persistence, operator review, approval, activation, and
   123	execution require distinct later authority and operational designs.
   124	
   125	## 8. References
   126

     1	# ADR-0007: Phase 6B persists exact advisory proposals for read-only preview
     2	
     3	Status: Accepted
     4	Date: 2026-07-20
     5	Deciders: Project architecture
     6	Affected volumes: Volume VIII §§2–9, 11; Volume XII
     7	Supersedes: None
     8	Superseded by: None
     9	
    10	## 1. Context and problem statement
    11	
    12	Phase 6A produces a pure immutable, non-authorizing follow-up proposal with a
    13	complete canonical identity. Operators need durable, repeatable inspection of
    14	that exact value. Persistence must not turn eligibility into approval or
    15	introduce activation, execution, scheduling, experiment creation, or follow-up
    16	authority. Reload must also reject database corruption rather than returning a
    17	mutable or partially validated approximation.
    18	
    19	## 2. Decision
    20	
    21	Phase 6B adds one append-only PostgreSQL manifest plus ordered member table,
    22	one collision-aware repository, a private validated hydration seam, and a
    23	read-only preview service.
    24	
    25	- The manifest and members preserve every public Phase 6A field exactly.
    26	- Canonical text is authoritative; the tagged hash only selects a lock/index
    27	  bucket. Same-hash/different-canonical proposals receive different storage
    28	  collision ordinals.
    29	- Exact retries return the existing row. A hash-scoped transaction advisory
    30	  lock serializes concurrent exact persistence.
    31	- Upstream approval/materialization/member triggers validate copied immutable
    32	  provenance, and a deferred trigger requires complete ordered membership.
    33	- Reload reconstructs the non-assignable Phase 6A object through one private
    34	  friend builder and reruns direct alignment plus full canonical/payload
    35	  invariants.
    36	- Preview runs under repeatable-read, read-only isolation and renders explicit
    37	  negative authority fields.
    38	- Runtime privileges are append-only and column-scoped. Phase 6B provides no
    39	  approval, activation, execution, queue, scheduler, experiment, or follow-up
    40	  authorization API or schema.
    41	
    42	## 3. Rationale and decision drivers
    43	
    44	- Preserve the identity produced by Phase 6A without parsing presentation
    45	  output or recomputing Phase 5 science/policy.
    46	- Make persisted corruption and duplicate exact identity fail closed.
    47	- Keep collision safety aligned with existing canonical-first repositories.
    48	- Make operator inspection useful while keeping it observably read-only.
    49	- Prevent persistence metadata such as row ID, collision ordinal, and creation
    50	  timestamp from changing proposal identity.
    51	
    52	## 4. Consequences
    53	
    54	### 4.1 Positive consequences
    55	
    56	- A persisted proposal reloads as the same immutable typed value.
    57	- Exact canonical and every upstream canonical/hash pair survive round trip.
    58	- Exact retries are idempotent and hash collisions do not merge identities.
    59	- Database constraints, triggers, privileges, and C++ hydration provide
    60	  defense in depth against incomplete or malformed records.
    61	- Preview cannot mutate lifecycle or scheduler state.
    62	
    63	### 4.2 Negative consequences and trade-offs
    64	
    65	- Full canonical provenance is duplicated and may approach the Phase 6A 1 MiB
    66	  ceiling.
    67	- Inserts depend on existing immutable Phase 4D approval/materialization rows.
    68	- Owner-level database corruption remains possible, but repository reload
    69	  detects it and fails closed.
    70	- Previewing full authoritative canonical text can produce large output.
    71	
    72	### 4.3 Risks and mitigations
    73	
    74	- Hash collision: lock/index by hash, then compare canonical text exactly and
    75	  retain a collision ordinal outside identity.
    76	- Partial manifest: insert in one transaction and enforce member completeness
    77	  with a deferred constraint trigger.
    78	- Authority creep: no decision/lifecycle schema or API and explicit false
    79	  safety fields in every preview record.
    80	- Mutable reconstruction: return the original const-field Phase 6A type and a
    81	  non-assignable persisted wrapper.
    82	
    83	## 5. Compatibility and migration
    84	
    85	Migration ``042`` is additive and depends on the existing Phase 4D approval
    86	and materialization tables. It does not alter experiment or scheduler tables.
    87	The Phase 6A public builder and canonical grammar remain version 1 and
    88	unchanged; constructor validation is strengthened for exact hydration.
    89	
    90	## 6. Verification and operational evidence
    91	
    92	- Repeatable migration, exact privilege, FK, trigger, index, and collation
    93	  assertions.
    94	- Exact round-trip, immutable reload, canonical/hash preservation, idempotent
    95	  duplicate replay, duplicate persisted identity rejection, and malformed row
    96	  rejection.
    97	- Preview content and repeatable-read/read-only behavior with an untouched
    98	  sequence sentinel.
    99	- Phase 6A, Phase 5A/B/C, relevant Phase 4D regression tests, Release build,
   100	  and whitespace audit.
   101	
   102	## 7. Alternatives considered
   103	
   104	### 7.1 Store only the proposal hash
   105	
   106	Rejected because hashes are not authoritative and cannot reconstruct or
   107	inspect exact provenance.
   108	
   109	### 7.2 Store only canonical text and parse it on every read
   110	
   111	Rejected because Phase 6A intentionally defines canonical generation, not a
   112	public parser, and normalized member rows support provenance constraints and
   113	bounded typed reload without making presentation text authoritative input.
   114	
   115	### 7.3 Return a mutable persistence DTO
   116	
   117	Rejected because callers could mistake reconstructed fields for a validated
   118	Phase 6A proposal and silently lose immutability guarantees.
   119	
   120	### 7.4 Add operator approval or execution state
   121	
   122	Rejected as a distinct later authority explicitly outside Phase 6B.
   123

     1	Phase 6B Recommendation Campaign Follow-Up Proposal Persistence and Preview
     2	===========================================================================
     3	
     4	Purpose
     5	-------
     6	
     7	Phase 6B durably records an already-built Phase 6A
     8	``RecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposal`` and provides a read-only operator
     9	preview of that persisted value.  It does not build or reinterpret a proposal,
    10	record an operator decision, approve follow-up, activate or execute anything,
    11	create an experiment, or interact with the scheduler.
    12	
    13	Schema
    14	------
    15	
    16	Migration ``042`` adds an append-only proposal manifest and an ordered member
    17	table.  The manifest stores the exact proposal version/canonical/hash triple,
    18	the exact assessment, policy, and policy-decision triples, complete campaign
    19	and materialization identities, the copied favorable/eligible/non-authorizing
    20	summary, reason, and member count.  The member table stores every ordered
    21	Phase 6A member identity, including nullable expected-experiment ID.
    22	
    23	Canonical columns use the bytewise PostgreSQL ``C`` collation.  The proposal
    24	canonical value retains the Phase 6A 1 MiB limit.  Tagged hashes have format
    25	checks but remain accelerators.  Exact canonical equality is authoritative.
    26	The pair ``(proposal_identity_hash, collision_ordinal)`` is unique, permitting
    27	same-hash/different-canonical values while the repository prevents duplicate
    28	exact canonicals under one hash-scoped transaction advisory lock.
    29	
    30	Restrictive foreign keys and invoker-rights insert triggers verify the exact
    31	immutable Phase 4D campaign approval, materialization, and ordered
    32	materialization-member provenance copied into the proposal.  A deferred
    33	constraint trigger requires a complete contiguous member set at commit.
    34	Runtime ``pqxx`` access is limited to ``SELECT``, column-scoped payload
    35	``INSERT``, and sequence ``USAGE``.  It has no ``UPDATE``, ``DELETE``,
    36	``TRUNCATE``, generated-ID, or generated-timestamp capability.
    37	
    38	Repository and immutable reload
    39	-------------------------------
    40	
    41	``PersistRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposal`` accepts only the immutable
    42	Phase 6A type.  It locks the tagged-hash bucket, compares exact canonical text,
    43	returns ``existing_identical`` for an exact retry, or inserts one manifest and
    44	all members in the caller's transaction.  Collision ordinals are repository
    45	metadata and never enter proposal identity.
    46	
    47	Find-by-ID and find-by-identity return
    48	``PersistedRecommendationCampaignFollowUpProposal``.  Its contained proposal
    49	is the original non-assignable Phase 6A value, not a mutable persistence DTO.
    50	A private friendship grants only the Phase 6B hydration builder access to the
    51	Phase 6A constructors.  Hydration reruns supported-version, canonical/hash,
    52	campaign, materialization, count, ordered-member, duplicate-member,
    53	eligibility, favorable-interpretation, false-authorization, summary, and full
    54	proposal-canonical/payload validation.  Malformed or incomplete persisted data
    55	therefore fails closed instead of yielding a partially trusted object.
    56	
    57	Read-only preview
    58	-----------------
    59	
    60	The preview service loads one persisted proposal in an explicit
    61	``REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY`` transaction.  It renders the complete
    62	authoritative proposal canonical text, all source identity hashes, summary,
    63	ordered members, persistence timestamp, and explicit negative authority
    64	fields.  Every preview record states that approval, activation, execution,

 - CLI parsing/validation/presentation outside scheduler polling.
 
 ### 4.2 Control flow
 
 Completed evidence → deterministic source selection → pure candidates →
 collision-aware persistence → optional explicit score/evaluation/ranking. The
 Phase 4C proposal → review → paused execution → activation chain consists of
 separately invoked and audited manual actions. Phase 4D reads ranking and Phase
 4C history to plan and review; campaign approval records only an explicit human
 decision and adds no implicit arrow to mutation or execution.
 
 The governed campaign path is:
 
 ```text
 recommendation ranking
 -> read-only campaign plan
 -> read-only campaign review
 -> explicit persisted campaign approval
 -> explicit approved-campaign materialization to Phase 4C proposals
 -> read-only exact campaign handoff
 -> explicit atomic Phase 4C proposal review for all exact campaign members
 -> either optional Phase 5 Step 1 execution then optional Step 2 activation
 -> or optional Phase 5 Step 3 atomic execution-and-activation launch
 -> existing scheduler lifecycle for ordinary pending experiments
 -> optional read-only Phase 5 Step 4 operational status snapshot
 -> optional read-only Step 5b outcome assessment
 -> optional pure Step 5c advisory policy interpretation
 -> optional pure Phase 6A follow-up proposal for later operator review
+-> optional exact Phase 6B persistence and read-only operator preview
 ```
 
 All displayed stages through exact proposal review are implemented through
 Phase 4D Step 6; Phase 4C execution and activation remain separately invoked
 actions. Phase 5 Step 1 invokes only the existing Phase 4C execution operation
 for the exact campaign membership. Phase 5 Step 2 separately invokes only the
 existing Phase 4C activation operation; neither step invokes the other.
 Phase 5 Step 3 is a separate command that reuses both transaction-bound
 authorities inside one transaction; it does not call either public command.
 Phase 5 Step 4 reads the immutable materialization and bounded downstream
 evidence only; it neither invokes Steps 1–3 nor contacts the scheduler process.
 Step 5b reuses that status lifecycle inside one read-only snapshot. Step 5c
 contains no repository or CLI and consumes only an already-built immutable
 assessment. Phase 6A consumes only the exact immutable assessment and policy
-decision and terminates at a non-authorizing proposal value.
+decision and terminates at a non-authorizing proposal value. Phase 6B may
+persist and preview only that exact value; it introduces no downstream action
+arrow.
 
 ### 4.3 Ownership boundaries
 
 Canonical text decides identity; repository transactions decide persistence;
 pure scoring, planning, campaign-review, outcome-policy, and follow-up-proposal
 components decide advisory output; pure review rules decide legal transitions;
 and the operator separately
 supplies review, conversion, and activation actions. Only Phase 4C Steps 4–5
 may create or activate the one provenance-linked experiment. Campaign
-planning, review, approval, outcome assessment, outcome policy, and Phase 6A
-follow-up proposal never do.
+planning, review, approval, outcome assessment, outcome policy, Phase 6A
+follow-up proposal, and Phase 6B persistence/preview never do.
 
 ## 5. Data model
 
 ### 5.1 Authoritative entities
 
 Recommendation policy, semantic/invocation configuration, recommendation scan,
 recommendation, score run/result/component, evaluation run/result/component,
 ranking snapshot/member, and review event.
 Conversion proposal, review decision, execution, activation, and campaign
 approval records are separate immutable audit entities; only their explicitly linked experiment is
 an experiment-lifecycle entity. Campaign plans and reviews are reconstructed,
 not persisted; Step 3 persists only their exact approved/rejected provenance.
 Campaign outcome assessments and policy decisions are point-in-time,
 non-persistent advisory values; their canonical identities bind exact upstream
 evidence but create no authoritative campaign decision.
-Phase 6A follow-up proposals are likewise non-persistent advisory values. Their
-canonical identities bind the exact assessment v2, policy v1, decision v1,
-campaign, materialization, ordered members, eligibility, and fixed
-non-authority semantics while excluding observation time.
+Phase 6A follow-up proposals are advisory values whose canonical identities
+bind the exact assessment v2, policy v1, decision v1, campaign,
+materialization, ordered members, eligibility, and fixed non-authority
+semantics while excluding observation time. Phase 6B persists that exact value
+in one immutable manifest and ordered member set; repository row ID, collision
+ordinal, and creation timestamp remain storage metadata outside identity.
 
 ### 5.2 Provenance and versions
 
 Canonical text is authoritative; tagged hashes accelerate lookup. Persisted
 records retain source experiment/analysis/model, scan, policy, identity,
 structural mutation, source rank, score policy/components, and review snapshot.
 
 ### 5.3 Invariants and legacy data
 
 Scan-associated rows require positive source rank and cannot detach from their
 originating scan. Proposed/approved identities remain active; rejected/expired
 matches remain historical blockers. Legacy NULL/NULL scan/rank rows are not
 backfilled and are excluded from operations requiring provenance.
 
 Review transitions are only proposed → approved, rejected, or expired. Review
 events are append-only to the runtime role. Approval is advisory and leaves
 `approved_experiment_id` null under Step 5.
 
 ## 6. Transactions
 
 ### 6.1 Read paths
 
 Evidence, list, detail, score history, evaluation history, ranking input, and
 review history use typed read-only repository paths. Ranking does not reopen
 source experiment metrics.
 
 ### 6.2 Write paths
 
 Candidate persistence uses short collision-aware transactions. Score result and
 ordered components persist atomically. Evaluation results and their unchanged
 Step 4 components persist atomically without locking experiment evidence.
 Review locks one recommendation and updates status plus one immutable event in
 the same transaction. Ranking persists its complete member set atomically and
 then completes a ranking-owned snapshot after an exact count check.
 Conversion-proposal insertion locks only its accelerator-hash bucket, compares
 canonical text exactly under the bytewise ``C`` collation, and inserts one
 complete row in one transaction. The collision ordinal is storage metadata;
 canonical text alone remains authoritative.
+Phase 6B proposal insertion locks only the proposal-hash bucket, compares
+authoritative canonical text exactly, inserts the manifest and ordered members
+in one caller-owned transaction, and enforces completeness at commit. It does
+not write any review, lifecycle, experiment, or scheduler table.
 
 ### 6.3 Failure semantics
 
 Invalid commands create no scan/event. Candidate failures are counted per scan.
 Score retries compare complete immutable results. Evaluation retains completed
 per-recommendation results if a later item fails, marks the run failed, and
 forbids adding new results to that terminal run; exact existing results remain
 verifiable. Review event failure rolls back status; terminal retries create no
 event. A ranking-member failure leaves no partial membership.
 
 ## 7. Concurrency
 
 ### 7.1 Conflict domain
 
 Generation conflicts on semantic configuration plus policy; scoring retries on
 score run plus recommendation; evaluation conflicts on canonical evaluation-run
 identity and evaluation run plus recommendation; ranking conflicts on canonical
 snapshot identity and snapshot plus evaluation result; review conflicts on one
 recommendation row.
 
 ### 7.2 Locking and serialization
 
 Generation uses a transaction advisory key plus canonical rechecks and active
 uniqueness. Scoring uses uniqueness and complete retry comparison. Evaluation
 uses a short shared lock on its own run row while inserting an atomic result;
 it does not lock experiment evidence. Review uses `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` and
 one-event uniqueness. Ranking serializes identical member verification with a
 short `FOR UPDATE` lock on its ranking-owned snapshot. Unrelated snapshots and
 unrelated work remain concurrent.
 
 ### 7.3 Winner, loser, and retry outcomes
 
 Concurrent identical generation returns one created/one existing result.
 Equivalent score retry reuses only an exact persisted result. Concurrent review
 produces one terminal winner and one `recommendation_review_status_conflict`;
 exactly one event exists. Concurrent identical ranking requests converge on one
 snapshot with an exactly verified member set.
 Concurrent identical conversion proposals converge on one exact canonical row;
 same-hash different canonical rows remain distinct.
+Concurrent identical Phase 6B proposal persistence converges on one exact
+canonical row; same-hash/different-canonical proposals receive distinct
+storage collision ordinals.
 
 ## 8. CLI
 
 ### 8.1 Commands and validation
 
 Generation, scoring, evaluation, ranking/comparison, their inspection commands,
 review actions, and review inspection are explicit families. Evaluation,
 ranking, and review mutation
 are mutually exclusive with generation, scoring, scheduler, continuation, and
 experiment-lifecycle commands.
 
 ### 8.2 Machine output
 
 `EXPERIMENT_RECOMMENDATION_*` records use stable fields, percent-escaped text,
 explicit `NULL`, deterministic ordering, and separate conflict/failure events.
 
 ### 8.3 Human output
 
 Human score/evaluation/review summaries are concise, control-byte safe, and
 state that the result is advisory and created/queued no experiment. Ranking
 separates advisory-ready, blocked, and non-actionable presentation.
+Phase 6B preview includes the full authoritative proposal identity, provenance,
+ordered members, and explicit false approval/activation/execution/scheduler
+fields in a read-only snapshot.
 
 ## 9. Testing
 
 ### 9.1 Pure tests
 
 Cover canonical identity/collisions, eligibility, candidates, scoring formulas,
 ranking, evaluation classification/identity, review parsing/reasons, and all
 transition outcomes. Phase 5 outcome tests additionally cover evidence
 classification, policy judgment, the advisory comparable-member evidence-
 coverage minimum, mixed member/metric states, locale independence,
 deterministic identity, and explicit non-authorization. The coverage minimum
 is not statistical sufficiency, confidence, causality, profitability,
 repeatability, or campaign success.
 Phase 6A pure tests additionally cover exact upstream alignment, stable refusal
 reasons, golden canonical identity, all non-authority flags, upstream-order,
 locale and observation-time invariance, identity sensitivity, inherited IEEE
 edge behavior, the canonical-size boundary, and inaccessible malformed
 construction paths.
+Phase 6B focused tests cover exact round trip, immutable typed reload,
+canonical/hash preservation, exact retry, duplicate persisted identity,
+malformed hash/member data, and read-only preview safety fields.
 
 ### 9.2 Persistence and migration tests
 
 Cover scans, duplicates, source rank/scan provenance, score ownership and
 immutability, review constraints, runtime privileges, SQLSTATEs, and migration
 repeatability. Evaluation tests additionally cover canonical idempotency,
 append-only result/component privileges, nullable blocked scores, and evidence
 foreign keys. Ranking tests cover exact membership, bucket/rank uniqueness,
 narrow privileges, scope/captured-membership trigger enforcement, bounded
 evidence loading, atomic member persistence, and Step 1 immutability.
 Conversion-proposal tests cover complete invocation round trips, exact retries,
 hash collisions, concurrent insertion, restrictive privileges, and unchanged
 experiment fixtures.
+Phase 6B migration/repository tests cover bytewise canonical storage,
+collision metadata, upstream provenance, deferred membership completeness,
+narrow append-only privileges, migration repeatability, malformed persistence
+rejection, and a preview read sentinel that remains untouched.
 
 ### 9.3 Concurrency and integration tests
 
 Cover same-candidate generation, score retries, evaluation run/result retries
 and partial failures, review action races, unrelated reviews, rollback, exact
 cleanup, and before/after experiment/identity/score digests.
 
 ### 9.4 Regression boundaries
 
 Steps 1–5 remain individually stable. Changes MUST NOT alter training,
 inference, continuation, experiment lifecycle, or scheduler behavior.
 
 ## 10. Operational safety
 
 ### 10.1 Runtime isolation
 
 No recommendation command enters scheduler polling. Integration uses disposable
 rows and exact cleanup without disturbing genuine experiments.
 
 ### 10.2 Permissions and destructive operations

 Phase 5 Step 5c adds a pure versioned policy over the Step 5a assessment. It
 uses the assessment's existing classifications and deltas, applies explicit
 metric-direction and advisory evidence-coverage rules, and separates evidence
 sufficiency, conservative interpretation, and eligibility for a later explicit
 operator review. Only a favorable, sufficient, all-comparable campaign is
 eligible for such review; neutral, unfavorable, mixed, and inconclusive
 campaigns are not. Its result is non-persistent and non-authoritative, always
 records follow-up authorization as false, and adds no repository, CLI,

 It validates authoritative canonical text as well as hashes and exact campaign,
 materialization, count, and ordered-member alignment. Only an eligible,
 favorable, explicitly non-authorizing decision yields a proposal. Contract v1
 binds every safety semantic and exact upstream canonical identity, excludes
 ``observedAt``, and rejects canonical text above 1,048,576 bytes before
 construction. The proposal is not approval, persistence, activation,
-execution, scheduler work, success evidence, or authority for Phase 6B–6F.
+execution, scheduler work, success evidence, or authority for later phases.

codex
I found a concrete identity defect: identity lookup filtered on both recomputed hash and canonical text. A corrupted row with the correct authoritative canonical but a wrong stored hash would be treated as absent, allowing persistence to create a second copy of the same canonical identity. I’m correcting lookup to select by authoritative `C`-collated canonical text alone and let hydration validate the stored hash fail-closed.

The review also found commit-blocking proof gaps around collision separation, deferred incomplete-member rollback, ordered-member trigger enforcement, concurrent exact insertion, and trigger-function privileges/canonical collations. I’m adding only focused negative/concurrency assertions to the existing Phase 6B tests; no production capability or design is changing.

One preview-test issue remained concrete: the existing untouched sentinel sequence was unrelated to the Phase 6B tables, so it could not detect accidental advancement of the proposal/member sequences. I’m tightening that assertion to snapshot the two actual Phase 6B sequence values immediately before and after both preview command paths. This is test-only and does not alter preview behavior.

+std::vector<long long> Phase6BSequenceValues(
+    pqxx::connection& owner,
+    const std::string& schema)
+{
+    pqxx::read_transaction transaction{owner};
+    const pqxx::result rows = transaction.exec(
+        "SELECT last_value FROM pg_sequences WHERE schemaname=$1 AND "
+        "sequencename<>'phase6b_preview_read_sentinel' ORDER BY "
+        "sequencename;", pqxx::params{schema});
+    std::vector<long long> values;
+    values.reserve(rows.size());
+    for (const auto& row : rows) values.push_back(row[0].as<long long>());
+    return values;
+}

+std::vector<long long> Phase6BSequenceValues(
+    pqxx::connection& owner,
+    const std::string& schema)
+{
+    pqxx::read_transaction transaction{owner};
+    const pqxx::result rows = transaction.exec(
+        "SELECT last_value FROM pg_sequences WHERE schemaname=$1 AND "

+        "sequencename;", pqxx::params{schema});
+    std::vector<long long> values;
+    values.reserve(rows.size());
+    for (const auto& row : rows) values.push_back(row[0].as<long long>());
+    return values;
